# Limitations

The claim is scoped to Gemma 3 270M, the PT+affine Gemma Scope 2
dictionary, occupation \(a\)/\(an\) prompts, and the interventions we ran.
The model is in a weak behavioral regime for this task. Outcomes are
lexical noun tokens, not semantic concepts. S1 was selected using article
and future-token attributions, so the paper identifies the causal
decomposition of this handle rather than the model's unique internal
ontology. S2 shares a feature with S1 and often derails rather than
flipping `an`; it is not a clean article-only dissociation. The S1 leftover
under `an` overlaps the random control, so we do not interpret it as a
specific noun plan. The 19-prompt article-switch subset is descriptive
because it conditions on an observed switch. TV distances are not additive
mediation effects. The seven-twin leftover estimate is small-\(N\).

The synthetic mediated/direct pair validates estimand polarity on a known
generative process; it is not a trained transformer and cannot replace the
Gemma stack-sensitivity control. The full-residual reference is patched at
the article-token position and therefore validates sensitivity of noun
computation there, not sensitivity of every pre-article planning site.
Large \(5\times\) sparse amplification may be off-manifold; affine skip
means sparse interventions need not exhaust MLP computation. Scale,
model-family, task, and sampling-policy generalization remain open.
